expect: Most people regain good shoulder movement over several weeks to months, with therapy guiding the pace. Your surgeon will give you your own timeline.

items.text: Ask a therapist about pre-surgery shoulder exercises
items.detail: Gentle range-of-motion and strengthening can help maintain muscle tone and make post-op rehab easier.

items.text: Ask if you will need a shoulder sling
items.detail: Some surgeons use a sling for comfort and others do not, and how long varies. Follow your surgeon's plan.
Ice for about 15 minutes at a time, up to a few times a day, with a cloth between the ice and your skin, can ease swelling and pain.

items.text: Plan for help with dressing and reaching overhead
items.detail: Your arm will be limited at first. Loose clothing helps, and you may need help with washing and hair. Dress the operated arm first.

items.text: Ask when physical therapy will start
items.detail: Simple gentle exercises often start right away, with an outpatient visit booked later. If you have not heard about an appointment within 2 weeks, contact the service.
Many people avoid the operated side, resting propped on their back or on the other side with pillows. Your surgeon may have advice about wearing a sling in bed.

items.text: Ask about lifting and carrying limits
items.detail: Heavy lifting and carrying are often limited for the first couple of weeks and repeated overhead activity for longer; the plan depends on what was done.

items.text: Ask which movements to avoid early on
items.detail: Overhead reaching, heavy lifting and sudden movements are commonly limited, but the rules depend on your procedure. Follow your surgeon's plan.

items.text: Ask exactly which version of the surgery you are having
items.detail: Arthroscopy can vary by side, repair type, and technique, and each may change your recovery plan.
How long varies from a few days to several weeks, and some surgeons ask you to wear it in bed. Your team will tell you when to stop.
Driving is often avoided for at least the first few weeks, until you are out of the sling and off strong pain medicine; your surgeon will advise.
Desk jobs may be possible within about a week, while heavy or overhead work usually needs longer; your surgeon will advise.
